deep_analysis.adaptation_guide: 1) Add NPU regression coverage for Qwen3-MoE (Qwen3MoeForCausalLM), Qwen3-Next and Qwen3.5 shared-expert/dense-MLP paths in BF16 and W8A8 static/dynamic modes to confirm Qwen3MoeMLP.forward still produces the same results after switching to maybe_fused_act_quant. 2) Verify the activation/quant interaction on NPU: fused_act_quant registers (SiluAndMul, kFp8StaticTensorSym) unconditionally, while dynamic FP8/NVFP4 entries are CUDA-gated. Confirm that AscendSiluAndMul/AscendSiluAndMul310 (subclasses, not exact SiluAndMul) and Ascend linear schemes never expose a matching _input_quant_key so maybe_fused_act_quant falls back to act_fn(x). If any Ascend W8A8/W8A8FP8 scheme starts exposing kFp8StaticTensorSym, add an NPU guard in vllm_ascend/ops/activation.py or the quant scheme/AdaptLinearMethod, or implement an NPU producer using npu_swiglu + _C_ascend quant instead of allowing the CUDA-only torch.ops._C.silu_and_mul_quant to run. 3) Audit vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/shared_experts.py: _can_fuse_w8a8_mxfp_activation and _shared_megamoe_activation_signature rely on the exact AscendSiluAndMul type and isinstance(act_fn, SiluAndMul); re-test after the maybe_fused_act_quant change and extend the checks if activation wrappers are introduced. 4) Add an end-to-end Qwen2-MoE test for Qwen/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B (mirroring examples/run_dp_server.sh) on the Transformers backend with TP/EP, and verify patch_attn_utils vllm-attention layout handling, the MoEBlockFuser path, AscendMoERunner/AscendRoutedExperts selection, weight loading, and quantization. 5) Update vllm-ascend documentation/support matrix and the example if Qwen2-MoE support is claimed, and run the existing patch_qwen3vl/patch_qwen3_5 unit tests since upstream qwen3_5 and qwen3_moe imports changed.
deep_analysis.risk: Medium. The signature additions to Qwen3MoeMLP are backward-compatible and vllm-ascend does not import the removed Qwen2MoeMLP, but the new maybe_fused_act_quant call changes the activation/quantization kernel-selection path for Qwen3-MoE and for the shared experts used by Qwen3-Next/Qwen3.5. On NPU, a CUDA-only static-FP8 producer is registered unconditionally; if an Ascend linear layer ever exposes kFp8StaticTensorSym, torch.ops._C.silu_and_mul_quant would be invoked and fail or produce wrong results. The default currently falls back because AscendSiluAndMul is not an exact type match and Ascend schemes do not set _input_quant_key, so this is a latent rather than immediate break, but it is fragile against future OOT/quant changes. Separately, Qwen2-MoE moving to TransformersMoEForCausalLM changes its weight-loading, attention and MoE execution path; EP/DP, quantization, and PP regressions are possible and should be validated end-to-end.

deep_analysis.adaptation_guide: The only code vllm-ascend actually consumes from this commit is vllm/models/minimax_m3/common/vision_tower.py, which minimax_m3_vl.py loads dynamically via _load_vllm_minimax_m3_common_module('vision_tower') and re-exports as MiniMaxVLVisionModel; tests/ut/models/minimax_m3/test_minimax_m3_vit.py even asserts source identity with that upstream file. After bumping vLLM past 92f3ee5: (1) verify the new MiniMaxVLVisionModel.load_weights (AutoWeightsLoader(self) + hf_to_vllm_mapper with orig_to_new_stacked '.q_proj.'/'.k_proj.'/'.v_proj.' -> '.qkv_proj.') still receives names with a leading-dot prefix from the vllm-ascend outer mapper in MiniMaxM3SparseForConditionalGeneration (which maps 'vision_tower.' -> 'model.vision_tower.'); if any checkpoint emits bare 'q_proj.weight', add an Ascend-side WeightsMapper/transform to normalize it, otherwise no code change is needed. (2) Add a unit test in tests/ut/models/minimax_m3/test_minimax_m3_vit.py that feeds '...self_attn.{q,k,v}_proj.weight' (and fused qkv_proj) through MiniMaxVLVisionModel.load_weights and asserts the qkv_proj shards plus projector/patch-merge weights load; there is currently no VL weight-loading e2e test. (3) Leave vllm_ascend/models/minimax_m3/minimax_m3.py::MiniMaxM3Model.load_weights unchanged: Ascend uses a fully independent text-model implementation (not the upstream amd/nvidia model), so the removed upstream hand-written loader, _redirect_fused_shared_experts, _mega_moe_expert_weight, ckpt_names=('w1','w2','w3') call sites and DeepGemmMegaMoEExperts.load_weights/l2_input_scale are NVIDIA/AMD-only and must NOT be ported. Ascend's MiniMaxM3MoE keeps shared experts as a separate MLP and its CANN MegaMoE quantization schemes manage their own scales, so the fused-shared-expert and fused '[E,...]' NVFP4 checkpoint handling has no NPU counterpart to update; only implement it later if Ascend needs the new RL weight-sync fused-expert checkpoint format.
deep_analysis.risk: Low. The upstream change is a behavior-preserving weight-loading refactor and the changed vision-tower file is inherited automatically, so there is no signature/contract change to NPUPlatform, NPUWorker, NPUModelRunner, attention backends, scheduler or communicator. deep_analysis.adaptation_guide: 1) In vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_speculative_config.py, reconcile _temporarily_disable_dspark_dcp with the new per-draft DCP field. The guard currently hides the target DCP during SpeculativeConfig.__post_init__, so _orig_post_init resolves draft_decode_context_parallel_size=1 even for full-attention MLA DSpark drafts; also an explicit draft DCP>1 is rejected by _verify_and_get_draft_dcp. Remove the guard now that upstream supports DSpark+DCP, or temporarily hide DCP only from the validations that need it and explicitly recompute/restore draft_decode_context_parallel_size to target DCP for full-attention MLA drafts and 1 for non-MLA/sliding-window drafts after post-init. Update the DSpark patch tests accordingly. 2) In vllm_ascend/worker/v2/spec_decode/pcp_utils.py::build_dspark_draft_config, keep the new field consistent when copying/adjusting the target parallel config; do not let the PCP=1 draft rewrite silently erase the resolved draft DCP. 3) In vllm_ascend/worker/v2/attn_utils.py::get_kv_cache_spec (which replaces vllm.v1.worker.gpu.model_runner.get_kv_cache_spec globally via patch_attn_utils), mirror the upstream draft-replication rule: for draft layers whose draft DCP resolves to 1 while target DCP>1, emit specs with dcp_sharded=False. This is required to avoid the SlidingWindowSpec 'DCP not support sliding window' assertion, wrong dcp_world_size in MLACommonMetadataBuilder, wrong reorder_batch_threshold, and wrong block-table/page accounting. Propagate dcp_sharded when rebuilding AscendMLAAttentionSpec/AscendSFAIndexerCacheSpec instead of constructing them with the default True, and preserve it through apply_dspark_resident_kv_specs. 4) In vllm_ascend/core/kv_cache_interface.py, make AscendMLAAttentionSpec.max_memory_usage_bytes honor self.dcp_sharded (mirror upstream FullAttentionSpec) instead of always dividing by the target DCP; add dcp_sharded to AscendSlidingWindowMLASpec.merge and AscendSFAIndexerCacheSpec.merge so grouped/rebuilt draft specs do not lose the replicated-cache flag. 5) In vllm_ascend/platform.py::_validate_draft_decode_context_parallel_config, validate the draft's actual draft_decode_context_parallel_size rather than the target's: skip GQA/MQA head/DCP checks when the draft is replicated at DCP=1, and use the per-draft value for max-DCP and head-divisibility checks. 6) In AscendDSparkSpeculator._init_dcp and AscendDFlash/Speculator paths, make sure the draft config seen by attn_vllm_config/current_vllm_config reflects the new field, and add an Ascend policy for upstream DFlashSpeculator.load_model's new windowed-layer ValueError if Ascend intends to run windowed SWA DSpark drafts at DCP>1 (otherwise force draft_decode_context_parallel_size=1 for them). 7) NIXL itself is not used by vllm-ascend, but if DCP-replicated draft caches are enabled with Ascend PD connectors, mirror the new get_dcp_replicated_group_ids/pull semantics (read the group from one DCP rank and end-trim remotely) or reject unsupported topologies explicitly.
deep_analysis.risk: High. A wrong or missing dcp_sharded flag is silent: the draft metadata builder may believe it is DCP-sharded under a DCP target while the draft actually runs replicated, leading to incorrect slot mapping/history lengths, wrong block-table sizing and memory accounting, or the SlidingWindowSpec assertion 'DCP not support sliding window'. The existing DSpark DCP patch can also silently disable DCP for full-attention MLA drafts (performance regression) or reject an explicit draft DCP, while non-MLA GQA draft validation may incorrectly apply the target DCP. Require coverage for both full-attention MLA DSpark+DCP and sliding-window DSpark under a DCP target, plus any PD/connector path, before relying on this upstream change.

deep_analysis.adaptation_guide:
1) Fix the load-time crash in vllm_ascend/models/deepseek_v41/engram/embedding.py: AscendParallelEngramEmbedding.__init__ calls nn.Module.__init__ directly and never sets self.peer_rows (upstream ParallelEngramEmbedding.__init__ does). The commit adds ParallelEngramEmbedding.process_weights_after_loading (vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py:1245), which begins with `if not self.peer_rows: return`. vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py::finalize_model_weights invokes every module's process_weights_after_loading, so all Ascend DeepSeek V4.1 Engram loads (default, rfork, netloader) will raise AttributeError: 'AscendParallelEngramEmbedding' object has no attribute 'peer_rows'. Either set `self.peer_rows = 0` (and defensively `self._peer_group = None`, `self._loaded = False`) in AscendParallelEngramEmbedding.__init__, or override process_weights_after_loading as a no-op in the Ascend subclass (Ascend's shared load already synchronizes writers via the all_gather in load_checkpoint). Add a unit test that runs finalize_model_weights or calls the hook on an Ascend table.
2) Handle the new config surface in vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_engram_config.py and vllm_ascend/platform.py::_validate_engram_config. Because the patch replaces verify_model_config/verify_parallel_config, upstream's new checks ('peer_group_size requires a DeepSeek V4.1 model', 'peer_group_size requires CUDA, TP=1, PP=1 and no elastic EP', group-size sanity) never run on Ascend. Since Ascend has no cuMem/FABRIC peer-table path (AscendParallelEngramEmbedding does not implement share_peer_table and the model never calls join_engram_peer_group), reject non-zero peer_group_size / non-null peer_group_store with a clear ValueError in _validate_engram_config (or in the patched validators), rather than silently accepting an ignored option. Keep the fields flowing through upstream EngramConfig for API compatibility, but do not claim support.
3) Preserve upstream's DeepSeek-only and cpu_offload=False constraints if ever relaxing the rejection; the base _validate_shared_memory still enforces pairing and cpu_offload, but the platform-level parallel checks are lost by the patch.
4) Update vllm-ascend tests/units (tests/ut/models/test_engram.py, tests/ut/patch/platform/test_patch_engram_config.py) to cover the new hook and the peer-group rejection, and note in docs/source/tutorials/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.md and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.md that peer_group_size/peer_group_store are CUDA-only and unsupported on Ascend. No action is needed for the engram_host_table -> engram_fabric_table rename because that import is guarded by current_platform.is_cuda() and Ascend never reaches it; the 128-row/PACKED kernel changes are bypassed by Ascend's own lookup implementation.
deep_analysis.risk: High functional impact but low-risk fix: unmitigated, the inherited hook crashes every Ascend DeepSeek V4.1 Engram weight load at model initialization (not at config validation), including CPU-offload and dp_shared_memory deployments. The config side is a silent-misconfiguration hazard because the Ascend validator patch hides upstream's new peer_group_size checks while the Ascend model ignores the feature, so users could believe tables are split across engines when they are not (potential OOM). The code change itself is small and localized to AscendParallelEngramEmbedding.__init__/hook override plus config validation; regression risk after the fix is low, provided a finalize_model_weights-based test is added.

deep_analysis.adaptation_guide: No mandatory vllm-ascend code change is required for the Step5 fix itself: there is no Ascend Step5 model, and NPUModelRunner V2 inherits GPUModelRunner.execute_model via super(), so both the Step5 make_empty_intermediate_tensors change (if Step5 is ever run through upstream) and the new PP validation are picked up automatically. Work is verification plus small alignment where needed: (1) Confirm target vllm-ascend V2 PP configs still pass after this commit. The new PPHandler.check_received_tensors is executed once per process on every non-first, non-dummy PP step, and raises ValueError if a buffer key is missing from the previous stage or if per-token shape[1:] differs; it warns (not fails) for unexpected keys and for dtype narrowing. (2) Audit each PP-capable Ascend model's make_empty_intermediate_tensors against what its forward actually returns to the next stage: keys must match exactly, shape[1:] must match, and dtype must match where precision matters. Pay special attention to FP32 residual streams: glm5next already declares post/comb as torch.float32; verify hidden_states/residual and any FP32 residual model (similar to Step5's fp32_residual_connection) declare float32 buffers instead of the default model dtype. (3) Audit vllm_ascend/worker/v2/pp_transport.py buffer factories used by patch/worker/patch_deepseek_v2.py (TOPK_INDICES in V2, AUX_HIDDEN_STATES in V1) and DeepSeek-V4/Kimi-K3 hc_mult-shaped hidden_states buffers: the topk_indices buffer is sliced as topk_indices_buffer[:batch_size], so its shape[1:] must equal the tensor the sender ships, and aux slot keys added by reserve_aux_intermediate_tensor_slots must be present on the receiving stage. (4) If a warning about dtype narrowing appears for an Ascend model that keeps FP32 residuals, update that model's buffer dtype to float32 rather than ignoring the warning; if a shape ValueError appears, fix the buffer shape (the old code silently broadcast trailing dims and silently rounded dtype). (5) Add/extend NPU PP tests analogous to tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py for missing-key, unexpected-key, shape-mismatch and dtype-narrowing cases, and run PP>1 (optionally with MTP/EAGLE3/DSpark) for DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, Kimi-K3, GLM-5.3-Flash and MiniMax-M3 on NPU. MRV1 is unaffected because the call site is in the V2 GPUModelRunner.
deep_analysis.risk: medium. The change is additive diagnostics in a shared V2 PP path, but it can convert previously silent behavior into a hard ValueError on NPU: the old copy path broadcast mismatched trailing dimensions and silently rounded dtype, while the new check rejects shape[1:] mismatches and missing keys on the first real (non-dummy) PP step. Ascend's custom PP transports (topk_indices buffer, aux hidden-state slots, hc_mult-shaped hidden states, FP32 residual/mHC post/comb) are exactly the places where key/shape/dtype declarations can diverge between adjacent pipeline stages, so latent mismatches may surface only at runtime with PP>1 and speculative decoding. The check is one-shot (guarded by PPHandler.checked_received_tensors) and does not change the actual copy/sampling logic, limiting blast radius, but failures would be fatal for PP serving, so PP+spec-decode NPU configurations should be validated before adopting this commit.

deep_analysis.adaptation_guide: The commit adds a new packed-MXFP4 Engram table format to upstream vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py, which vllm-ascend directly imports (EngramLayout) and subclasses (ParallelEngramEmbedding). 1) In vllm_ascend/models/deepseek_v41/model.py (~L1052-L1090) read layout.packed_fp4/layout.row_bytes from upstream EngramLayout and pass a packed_fp4 flag into AscendParallelEngramEmbedding; make engram_storage_dtype recognize the MXFP4 checkpoint dtype (uint8/U8) and return torch.uint8 instead of falling through to INT8 requantization, and bypass the non-A5 native_mxfp8->INT8 fallback for packed tables (or reject FP4 explicitly). 2) In embedding.py add packed_fp4/row_bytes to AscendParallelEngramEmbedding.__init__ and keep it call-compatible with the upstream signature; allocate weight as (part_num_embeddings, dim//2) uint8 and scales as (part_num_embeddings, dim//32) uint8; extend _load_into_storage to copy packed bytes bit-exactly without dequantize/requantize; extend _torch_lookup to decode E2M1 nibbles (even column = low nibble, e==0 => m*0.5); keep the output as BF16 and reject the FP8 packed-output path. 3) In npu.py use dim//2 as the row width with uint8 for HostUvaBuffer/SharedUvaBuffer and the gather helpers so CHUNK_ROWS offsets are based on packed row bytes; ensure the BF16 exchange still works after dequantization. 4) In ops/triton/engram_lookup.py add PACKED_FP4 handling and E2M1 decode to both _engram_int8_gather_dequant_kernel and _engram_host_uva_gather_dequant_kernel, preserving the existing UE8M0 scale decode and group-32 scales, and loading uint8 bytes rather than float8. 5) Add tests mirroring upstream test_engram_mxfp4_lookup_matches_torch/test_engram_packed_weight_is_half_width_uint8 across cpu_offload and dp_shared_memory. If MXFP4 Engram is intentionally out of scope for Ascend, at minimum accept packed_fp4 in the Ascend constructor and fail fast before allocating tables with a clear unsupported-format error.
deep_analysis.risk: Medium: E2M1 nibble order and UE8M0 scale semantics must match upstream bit-for-bit or lookups silently produce wrong values; using dim instead of dim/2 breaks packed row strides and host-UVA chunk offsets; uint8 packed tables can be mistaken for INT8/MXFP8 and dequantized/requantized into garbage; Ascend has no native FP4 path, so the Triton-Ascend device and host-UVA kernels need validation on A2/A3/A5; existing BF16/INT8/MXFP8 Engram paths must not regress. The Ascend subclass overrides upstream __init__, so any future upstream caller passing packed_fp4 will raise TypeError until the kwarg is added.

commits.comment: 修复 DSpark 自适应验证在 TP ranks 间可能选出不同 batch 布局的问题：`AdaptiveVerificationManager` 在计算 `draft_budget`（argmax 估计接受 token/成本的比）后新增 `get_tp_group().broadcast_object(draft_budget, src=0)`，在 `reallocate_drafts` 写入每请求容量后新增 `get_tp_group().broadcast(capacities, src=0)`。原因是各 rank 的 draft confidence 可能差 1 个 fp32 ULP，在 tie 或边界处会选不同请求，导致各 rank 的 cu_num_logits/query_start_loc 不一致甚至 hang。测试用 gloo 多进程（2/4 rank）构造 ULP 差异与置信度交换两种场景，断言各 rank layout 一致，并通过 monkeypatch 屏蔽 device communicator 与 Triton kernel。新增的是集合通信而非接口签名变更，正确性收益明显；代价是每步多两次 TP 集合通信（broadcast_object/broadcast），需保证在 CUDA graph 捕获/重放与 DBO 路径下不被破坏。

ascend_impact.functionality: `AdaptiveVerificationManager`（vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/adaptive_verification.py）现在在每一步通过 `get_tp_group().broadcast_object(draft_budget)` 和 `get_tp_group().broadcast(capacities)` 强制 TP ranks 一致；vllm-ascend v2 model runner 的 speculator 层（vllm_ascend/worker/patch_v2/patch_*_speculator.py 与 vllm_ascend/spec_decode）若复用/复制该类，则在 NPU 上由 HCCL 的 TP GroupCoordinator 承担这两次广播，patch 副本必须同步加入同样的广播，否则各 NPU rank 的 draft budget 与适配容量仍会分叉并导致 SchedulerOutput/attention metadata 布局不一致。
ascend_impact.testing: vLLM 侧新增的 gloo 多进程测试与被测逻辑平台无关，可作为 NPU 侧的对照基线；vllm-ascend 需要覆盖 HCCL TP 组下 broadcast_object/broadcast 的返回值一致性，以及 FULL graph 捕获/重放与 DBO 多 ubatch 场景下广播位置不引入额外同步点导致卡死。

All TP ranks within a DP replica share the scheduler output, so they should enter both calls in lockstep; however Ascend DP idle/dummy-rank and profiling paths must be checked so no rank skips get_num_tokens/reallocate_drafts. Also verify collective ordering with Triton budget assignment and ACL graph replay. broadcast_object is already used by set_cost_curves in this module, so the CPU/gloo path is proven on Ascend; the HCCL broadcast of capacities is the main new item to validate. deep_analysis.adaptation_guide: This commit removes the hard-coded name set `_KV_CACHE_REGISTERING_CONNECTORS` and `uses_nixl_on_device_memory()`; registration/export is now declared by each connector class via the new `KVConnectorBase_V1.kv_cache_access(kv_transfer_config) -> KVCacheAccess` classmethod. The default is `KVCacheAccess.IN_PROCESS`, so vllm-ascend's RDMA-registering connectors are now silently misclassified (they declare nothing). Add a `@classmethod kv_cache_access` override (import `KVCacheAccess` from `vllm.config.kv_transfer`) to the connectors that register device KV cache with a transfer engine: MooncakeConnector (kv_p2p/mooncake_connector.py, mooncake/connector.py base, mooncake_hybrid_connector.py, mooncake_layerwise_connector.py, mooncake_d2rh_connector.py), AscendStoreConnector, and SfaRemoteD2HConnector -> return `KVCacheAccess.REGISTERS` (they call `global_te/m_store/memfabric.register_buffer`). For UCMConnectorV1 decide based on its export path: `REGISTERS` if RDMA-registered, add `EXPORTS_FABRIC`/`EXPORTS_FD` if it hands device memory to another process (NIXL/cuda_ipc style). Do NOT override the pure in-process connectors (AscendOffloadingConnector, AscendSimpleCPUOffloadConnector, PreemptOffloadConnectorV1); `IN_PROCESS` is correct. `AscendMultiConnector` needs no override because it inherits `MultiConnector.kv_cache_access`, which builds each child's `KVTransferConfig` and ORs the flags; just verify each child config name/class-name alias resolves through the factory. Add unit tests mirroring upstream `test_kv_transfer_registers_kv_cache_memory`/`test_external_connector_kv_cache_access` for names like `MooncakeConnectorV1`, `MooncakeConnectorV2`, `AscendStoreConnector`, `SfaRemoteD2HConnector`, including a MultiConnector case. Also note the new eager behavior: `VllmConfig._resolve_extensible_kv_cache` now calls `kv_transfer_config.kv_cache_access()` unconditionally (even on NPU, where extensible KV cache is later marked unsupported), so the connector class (and its module-level `from mooncake.engine import TransferEngine`) is imported during config resolution in every process; ensure these imports are available/guarded. No vllm-ascend code references the removed `uses_nixl_on_device_memory`; `registers_kv_cache_memory()` still exists and now delegates to `kv_cache_access().needs_single_chunk()`.
deep_analysis.risk: Low-to-medium. On current Ascend, `enable_extensible_kv_cache` is always disabled because `current_platform.is_cuda_alike()` is False, so a missing override only changes `registers_kv_cache_memory()` from false to false (latent, not a current runtime failure). Risk rises if extensible KV cache / single-chunk KV allocation is later enabled for NPU: wrongly returning the default `IN_PROCESS` would let the VMM/extensible cache allocate segments the Mooncake/AscendStore/SFA RDMA engines cannot register, and could affect block-compaction/defrag decisions. A second risk is the new config-time eager connector import: vllm-ascend Mooncake modules import the optional `mooncake` package at module import, so environments where `kv_connector` is set but `mooncake` is not importable in the scheduler/frontend process may now fail during `VllmConfig` construction instead of at connector initialization.

deep_analysis.adaptation_guide: 1) Add an Ascend override of context_kv_modules for DFlashQwen3Model in vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_qwen3_dflash.py. The current Ascend replacement of precompute_and_store_context_kv reads self.layers[i].self_attn.k_norm directly, but upstream DFlashQwen3Model.context_kv_modules() keeps only hidden_norm, layer.self_attn.attn (inner Attention), fc, and the fused/_context_kv_proj/_context_qkv_projs. k_norm lives on the outer self_attn wrapper and is therefore not retained, so free_unused_weights will empty it and the Ascend context-KV writer will fail or write corrupted K. Return the upstream list plus [layer.self_attn.k_norm for layer in self.layers]. Also keep _context_qkv_projs when _fused_kv_weight is None even if _context_kv_proj exists, because the Ascend _project_context_kv ignores the MXFP8 _context_kv_proj branch and uses _context_qkv_projs; alternatively port the _context_kv_proj branch into the Ascend implementation. This override must apply to Qwen3DSparkModel, DFlash2Qwen3Model, LiLiCorr, and AscendQwen3DSparkForCausalLM, which inherit the DFlash context path. 2) For Ascend-only DSpark backbones (Glm5DSparkModel, AscendK3DSparkModel, DeepseekV4/V41DSparkModel), either implement context_kv_modules listing exactly the modules their custom precompute/combine path reads (context_proj/context_norm, fused_qkv_a_proj / kv_a_proj_with_mqa, kv_norm, context_wkv_proj, per-layer attn wrappers, rotary buffers stay as buffers) or deliberately leave the hook absent so free_unused_weights is a no-op. AscendK3DSparkModel currently inherits upstream K3DSparkModel (plain nn.Module, no hook), so it is safe but gets no memory saving; the DFlashQwen3Model-derived paths are the ones at real risk. 3) Mirror upstream scheduling semantics in NPUModelRunner (vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py): use vllm_config.num_scheduled_spec_tokens (0 in prefill_context_kv_only) instead of self.num_speculative_steps for decode_query_len, AscendRequestState.num_speculative_steps, query_per_req, PCP/DCP and profiling/dummy-run shapes, and draft scheduling. Keep num_speculative_tokens only where static capacity/PP transport really needs it. Because NPUModelRunner.load_model wraps super().load_model, verify the new speculator.free_unused_weights(self.model) call runs after Ascend post_process/weight alignment and pd_dspark_aux_layer_ids capture, and that Ascend does not re-register the speculator in EPLB when context-only. 4) In AscendDFlashSpeculator/AscendDSparkSpeculator ensure context_kv_only is propagated through config copies (build_dspark_draft_config/replace) and that no Ascend load hook (post_process, _lmhead_tp_wrap_draft_logits, DSpark context init) reads draft weights after free_unused_weights. 5) Audit NPUWorker weight-update paths: inherit or mirror upstream's supports_draft_weight_updates=false and the RuntimeError start_draft_weight_update guard for prefill_context_kv_only. 6) Audit Ascend scheduler variants: they consume self.num_spec_tokens, which now comes from VllmConfig.num_scheduled_spec_tokens; replace any direct speculative_config.num_speculative_tokens reads used for scheduling/lookahead, and handle DFlashSpeculatorConfig.num_lookahead_tokens()==0 and max_num_draft_seqs()==None. 7) Confirm patch_speculative_config.py preserves prefill_context_kv_only through the DSpark DCP/config rewrites and that the new kv_producer validation is compatible with Ascend PD connectors (or explicitly reject the option if Ascend's SFA-PD/Mooncake context path is not wired to this hook).
deep_analysis.risk: High when the flag is enabled, low when left at the default false. The main hazard is silent under-retention: Ascend's patched DFlash context-KV writer reads k_norm (and, for quantized drafts, _context_qkv_projs) which upstream context_kv_modules does not keep; free_unused_weights replaces those params with 0-element tensors, causing shape/runtime errors or, worse, corrupted context K/V transferred to decode instances. Ascend-only DSpark backbones without the hook are safe but silently lose the memory benefit. A second hazard is runner/scheduler divergence: scheduler schedules 0 draft tokens and reserves no lookahead slots while NPUModelRunner still derives decode_query_len/request-state/dummy shapes from num_speculative_tokens, which can break ACL graph capture/replay, PP/PCP/DCP metadata, and warmup shapes. Mitigate by adding Ascend regression tests equivalent to test_context_kv_modules (K/V unchanged after free_unused_weights) plus a prefill_context_kv_only scheduler/model-runner smoke test.
